tutorial.title: Making Decisions
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn to write smart programs that  adapt to different situations.

lessons.title: Adapt to situations
lessons.interactiveContent: Smart programs use booleans to make decisions on whether to run lines of code or skip them.

lessons.title: If statement
lessons.interactiveContent:
We use an if statement to write code that responds to different situations. We recognize it by the keyword if.

Make sure to type if.

lessons.title: If statement
lessons.interactiveContent:
The if statement runs code only if it is evaluated as true. It's like saying, if something is true, then do this.

Let's make the evaluation true by simply using the boolean value True to display "Hello" in the console.

Make sure to pick True.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The if statement runs code only if it is evaluated as true. It's like saying, if something is true, then do this.

Pick the boolean value and the punctuation that make this display Hello! in the console.

Make sure to pick True, followed by :.

lessons.title: If statement
lessons.interactiveContent:
But what if we want to skip the code? In that case, we need the statement to evaluate as false.

Let's easily make the statement evaluate to false by simply using the boolean value False. Nothing will print.

Make sure to type False.

lessons.title: Conditions
lessons.interactiveContent:
Values like True are called conditions. Statements relying on conditions are called conditionals.

Conditions decide if the code runs or gets skipped. They come in between if and the colon :.

Make sure to pick if, followed by True, and finally :.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Values like True are called conditions. Statements relying on conditions are called conditionals.

Conditions decide if the code runs or gets skipped. Build the line so it displays Hello.

Make sure to pick if, followed by True, and finally :.

lessons.title: Code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
if statements don't decide on skipping or running the entire code. They only make decisions about a code block.

Make sure to pick print("I'm a code block!").
lessons.hardModeContent:
if statements don't decide on skipping or running the entire code. They only make decisions about a code block.

Build the block so it displays I'm a code block!.

Make sure to pick print, followed by "I'm a code block!".

lessons.title: Code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
We use an indentation of two spaces to highlight code blocks, like indenting this display statement.

Indentation refers to the space between the code and the code editor's margin.

Make sure to pick print("I'm two spaces away!").
lessons.hardModeContent:
We use an indentation of two spaces to highlight code blocks, like indenting this display statement.

Indentation refers to the space between the code and the code editor's margin. Finish the line so it prints I'm two spaces away!.

Make sure to pick "I'm two spaces away!".

lessons.title: Code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
A code block can be more than a one-liner. All lines with the same indentation belong to the same code block.

We can see it here when we use print() to add one more line at the beginning.

Make sure to pick print, followed by "Look at me!".
lessons.hardModeContent:
A code block can be more than a one-liner. All lines with the same indentation belong to the same code block.

We can see it here when we use print() to add one more line at the beginning.

Add the first line so the console shows Look at me! above I'm a code block.

Make sure to pick print, followed by "Look at me!".

lessons.title: Indentation Error
lessons.interactiveContent:
If the indentation is incorrect, the computer can't understand your code. This leads to an IndentationError showing up in the console.

Here, the second print() is wrongly indented by only one space instead of two, like the first print().

Make sure to pick print.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If the indentation is incorrect, the computer can't understand your code. This leads to an IndentationError showing up in the console.

Here, the second print() is wrongly indented by only one space instead of two, like the first print(). Restore the display call.

Make sure to pick print.

lessons.title: True Variable
lessons.interactiveContent:
Instead of using the boolean True, we can save it in a variable like greet and use it as the condition.

Make sure to type greet.

lessons.title: False variable
lessons.interactiveContent:
Using a variable like greet set to False allows us to skip code like the display statement.

Make sure to pick False.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Using a variable like greet as the condition lets us skip code like the display statement.

Assign the value that makes the if statement skip its display statement.

Make sure to pick False.

lessons.title: Question 1: Code Block

What do we call the code that is indented after an if statement?

A code blockAn if statement

A code block.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Several lines share the same indentation under an if statement. What do those lines form together?

A code blockAn if statementA condition

Make sure to pick A code block.

lessons.title: Question 2: Code Block 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we know that print("Low battery") is not inside the if statement?

Because of its indentationBecause the if statement can't have more lines in its code block

Because of its indentation.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The code below displays Low battery.

Now imagine you add two spaces in front of print("Low battery") so it lines up with print("Charged"). What would that new version display?

Nothing, because both display lines would be inside the skipped block.Low battery, because that line would still be outside the block.An error, because an if block can contain only one line.

Nothing, because both display lines would be inside the skipped block.

lessons.title: Question 3: Indentation Error
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

The two print() statements inside the if block don't have the same indentation, so the console will show an IndentationError messageThere's nothing wrong with the code

The two print() statements inside the if block don't have the same indentation, so the console will show an IndentationError message.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You want both messages to stay inside the if block. Which change fixes the code?

Give both print() lines the same indentation.Move the second print() line all the way to the left.Remove the colon after if True.

Give both print() lines the same indentation.

lessons.title: Question 4: Expand code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the maximum number of lines that a code block can have?

As many as we wantOne

As many as we want.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You need three display lines to run when one condition is true. Can all three lines belong to the same code block?

Yes, a code block can contain as many lines as needed.No, a code block can contain only one line.Only if each line has different indentation.

Yes, a code block can contain as many lines as needed.
